5	## What the matrix inherits from the family
6	
7	The matrix is written in the requirements genre `docs/spec-format.md` defines, and every law that page states holds here unchanged:
8	
9	- the closed-vocabulary glossary, so every domain noun the matrix uses carries one glossary entry under one name;
10	- the criterion form, so the keywords *when*, *while*, *if*, *then*, and *shall* are set in lowercase italics, no word stands in all capitals outside a code anchor, and the code anchor trails at the line's end;

12	- the generated-section gating, so a section a script builds is output only and a gate reds a hand edit of it;
13	- the comprehension gate, so a changed section clears the mechanical lints and then a panel of cold readers, passing only after two consecutive reads return zero blocking findings.
14	
15	A reader who needs any of these consults `docs/spec-format.md`. The rest of this page adds the parts the matrix carries that the spec does not.
16	
17	## What the matrix is
18	
19	The matrix is the spec projected into a checkable grid. It is derived from the proven spec through the proven architecture, and the spec keeps sole authority over what is true; a fact the matrix carries that the spec does not is a derivation defect. The matrix answers one question the spec does not: for each fact the spec states, which test holds it, pinned at which level, and whether that test exists yet.
20	
21	## Document structure
22	
23	TEST_MATRIX.md is the matrix's core, not its whole body. The core opens with a short preamble, the same shape the family gives it: what the document covers, what the bracket codes are, and how the keywords read. Two things follow the preamble, in this order:
24

27	
28	The matrix rows — the body, grouped into node blocks — live outside the core, one file per architecture node under `matrix/`, never inside TEST_MATRIX.md. The generated Reference, mapping each spec anchor to the matrix rows that cover it, lives outside the core too, in its own committed file, `TEST_MATRIX.index.md`.
29	
30	A reader who wants the whole matrix as one document reads it through the shared reader rather than opening TEST_MATRIX.md alone. `guardrails/specformat.py`'s `spec_paths()` and `read_document()` join the core and the parts the Parts map names into one body, in map order, the same join the spec's own core and parts already use; a gate or a builder script takes the core, then each part, on its command line, and reads them this way. The spec anchor the row derives from trails at the sentence's end, the family's criterion form, and it is the row's parent fact — the Reference the matrix generates reads the row's coverage from that trailing anchor.
35	
36	A converted row carries five cells: the row id, the fact sentence with its trailing anchors, the pinned level, the owning test, and the status. The spec-reference column the pre-conversion grid carried folds into the trailing anchors, so the anchors are parsed from the trailing brackets of the fact sentence.
37	
38	Beside the criterion the row carries three fields the spec criterion has no need of:
39	
40	- **the pinned level** — the rung the row's test sits at, drawn from the project's declared level ladder. The level is the row's most important judgment, and the family's criterion form does not carry it, so the matrix row states it as its own field. The ladder's rungs are named by what proves them, so each project kind fills them with its own concrete proof artifacts, declared at founding, and the row pins one of its own project's rungs.
41	- **the owning test** — the test that holds this row, named so a reader walks from the fact to the test that proves it.
42	- **the status** — one of *built* (the test exists and runs green), *todo* (the test's future owner is named in the row), or *retired* (the row is kept, never deleted).
43	
44	A matrix-local row id is legal, and the spec anchor stays the parent. One spec fact may project into several separately-testable rows, and a node's own mechanics may carry their own contract rows; an audit finding that a matrix row id is absent from the spec is expected for these, since the anchor the row cites is the parent fact, not the row id.
45	
46	## Node blocks stand as the case grouping
47	
48	The spec groups its criteria into named cases. The matrix groups its rows into node blocks: one block per architecture node, headed `### [node: <name>]`, and the block heading is the matrix's case grouping. Each node block is its own file under `matrix/`, named after the node with any `[target]` marker dropped from the filename only, never from the heading text: a node the architecture marks `[target]` — promised under an owned queue row, its machinery not yet landed — keeps that mark in its block heading, so the matrix and the architecture read the same. A new row is written into its node's own part file under `matrix/`, the file the Parts map names for that node, never into TEST_MATRIX.md.
49	
50	The spec criterion sits inside a requirement that gives it a Context block and a User Story; the matrix row carries neither. The fact's Context and its User Story live once at the spec, and the row inherits them through its trailing anchor. Restating them on the row would give one fact a second home, so the row stands down from carrying them and points at the spec instead.
51	
52	## The generated Reference
53	
54	The Reference maps each spec anchor to the matrix rows covering it. Its committed home is `TEST_MATRIX.index.md`, a file of its own beside the core, the same home `PRODUCT_SPEC.index.md` gives the spec's own Reference. `scripts/build-matrix-reference.py` builds it from the body rows at freeze, reading each row's trailing anchors and its row id across the core and every part the Parts map names, and the file is output only; no one edits it by hand. The builder reads a row's anchors the way the suite reads them today: a row may cite several codes, each mapped, and a range anchor of the form `T-1..T-7` expands to its members before mapping.
55	
56	A gate holds the Reference against drift, `guardrails/check-matrix-reference.py`, a sibling of `guardrails/check-index-generated.py`. It takes the core, then each part, then the committed index path, on its command line, and it reds on three faults:
57	
58	- the committed Reference differs from a fresh build off the current body — a hand edit, or a body that moved without a rebuild;
59	- a spec anchor sits on a body row and is absent from the committed Reference;
60	- a spec anchor sits in the committed Reference and is carried by no body row.
61	
62	When it passes it states its reach on the green line — the files it opened and the rows it matched of the rows it scanned — the reach every gate in this family states.
63	
64	## The row lint
65	
66	The coverage checklist the matrix once walked by hand is promoted to a mechanical row lint. The lint reads every body row and reds a row that pins no level from the declared level ladder, or that states no never side — the row's forbidden half, found by the literal word *never* in the fact sentence. 67

69	
70	The two checklist items the lint now holds — a level pinned per row, a never side present per row — leave the hand-walked checklist, and the checkbox gate that read that checklist retires with it. 73	
74	One delivery converts the whole matrix to this format, and everything that reads the old shape moves in that same delivery:
75	
76	- **The traceability reader is rebuilt beside the rows.** The suite's matrix reader, `matrix_blocks()` in `tests/test_traceability.py`, today requires six cells per row and reads the anchors from the third cell. 81

    24	  `crit.pieces` returns the criterion's own body first and then each bullet. The sub-list ends at the

    80	class Bullet(object):
    81	    """One indented bullet under a criterion line, carrying a piece of that criterion's rule."""
    82	
    83	    def __init__(self, text, line_no, index):

    94	class Criterion(object):
    95	    def __init__(self, req_num, number, text, line_no):

    97	        self.number = number            # its own criterion number (int)
    98	        self.text = text                # the full criterion text after "N. "
    99	        self.line_no = line_no          # 1-based source line
   100	        self.case = None                # the case name it sits under (or None)
   101	        self.gap_lines = []             # any [GAP: ...] lines recorded beneath it
   102	        self.bullets = []               # Bullet objects of its sub-list, in order
   103	
   104	    @property
   105	    def codes(self):
   106	        """The distinct codes in this criterion's trailing anchor, ranges kept whole."""
   107	        anchor = self.anchor

   110	    @property
   111	    def anchor(self):

   143	class Requirement(object):

   175	def parse(text):
   176	    """Parse a requirements-format document into a Document. Tolerant: unknown lines are ignored, so
   177	    a partly-formed document still yields the structure the gates can red against."""
   178	    doc = Document()
   179	    doc.text = text
   180	    lines = text.split("\n")
   181	
   182	    # Locate the glossary heading (the first of the two forms that appears).
   183	    gloss_idx = None
   184	    for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
   185	        s = ln.strip()
   186	        if s in GLOSSARY_HEADS:
   187	            gloss_idx = i
   188	            doc.glossary_head = s
   189	            break
   190	
   191	    # Preamble: everything before the glossary heading (or before the first requirement if no
   192	    # glossary heading is present).
   193	    first_req = None
   194	    for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
   195	        if REQUIREMENT_RE.match(ln.strip()):
   196	            first_req = i
   197	            break
   198	    cut = gloss_idx if gloss_idx is not None else (first_req if first_req is not None else len(lines))
   199	    doc.preamble = "\n".join(lines[:cut]).strip()
   200	
   201	    # Glossary terms: from the glossary heading up to the first requirement (or the next `## ` head).
   202	    if gloss_idx is not None:
   203	        for i in range(gloss_idx + 1, len(lines)):
   204	            s = lines[i].strip()
   205	            if REQUIREMENT_RE.match(s) or (s.startswith("## ") and s not in GLOSSARY_HEADS):
   206	                break
   207	            m = GLOSSARY_TERM_RE.match(lines[i])
   208	            if m:
   209	                doc.glossary.append((m.group(1).strip(), m.group(2).strip(), i + 1))
   210	
   211	    # Requirements, cases, criteria.
   212	    cur_req = None
   213	    cur_case = None
   214	    in_ac = False
   215	    last_crit = None
   216	    bullet_owner = None                 # the criterion whose sub-list is open here
   217	    prev_blank = True
   218	    for i, raw in enumerate(lines):
   219	        s = raw.strip()
   220	        if not s:
   221	            prev_blank = True
   222	            continue
   223	        if prev_blank and raw[:1] not in (" ", "\t"):
   224	            # A blank line and then unindented text close the open sub-list.
   225	            bullet_owner = None
   226	        prev_blank = False
   227	        mreq = REQUIREMENT_RE.match(s)
   228	        if mreq:
   229	            cur_req = Requirement(int(mreq.group(1)), mreq.group(2).strip(), i + 1)
   230	            doc.requirements.append(cur_req)
   231	            cur_case = None
   232	            in_ac = False
   233	            last_crit = None
   234	            bullet_owner = None
   235	            continue
   236	        if cur_req is None:
   237	            continue
   238	        if CONTEXT_RE.match(s):
   239	            cur_req.has_context = True
   240	            continue
   241	        if USER_STORY_RE.match(s):
   242	            cur_req.has_user_story = True
   243	            continue
   244	        if AC_RE.match(s):
   245	            cur_req.has_ac = True
   246	            in_ac = True
   247	            continue
   248	        mcase = CASE_RE.match(s)
   249	        if mcase:
   250	            cur_case = mcase.group(1).strip()
   251	            cur_req.cases.append(cur_case)
   252	            last_crit = None
   253	            bullet_owner = None
   254	            continue
   255	        # A [GAP: ...] line attaches to the criterion above it.
   256	        if GAP_RE.search(s) and CRITERION_RE.match(raw) is None:
   257	            if last_crit is not None:
   258	                last_crit.gap_lines.append(s)
   259	            continue
   260	        mcrit = CRITERION_RE.match(raw)
   261	        if mcrit and in_ac:
   262	            crit = Criterion(cur_req.number, int(mcrit.group(2)), mcrit.group(3).strip(), i + 1)
   263	            crit.case = cur_case
   264	            cur_req.criteria.append(crit)
   265	            last_crit = crit
   266	            bullet_owner = crit
   267	            continue
   268	        # An indented bullet under an open criterion is a piece of that criterion.
   269	        mbul = BULLET_RE.match(raw)
   270	        if mbul and bullet_owner is not None:
   271	            bullet_owner.bullets.append(
   272	                Bullet(mbul.group(1).strip(), i + 1, len(bullet_owner.bullets) + 1))
   273	            continue
   274	    return doc

   277	def normalize_criterion(text):
   278	    """The delta-classifier normal form (SPEC INV-261): whitespace collapsed, italic `*` markers
   279	    stripped, letters case-folded OUTSIDE code anchors — so a `[INV-4]` anchor keeps its case while
   280	    the sentence around it folds. Bracketed groups are held verbatim, the rest is folded."""
   281	    parts = re.split(r"(\[[^\]]*\])", text)
   282	    out = []
   283	    for j, part in enumerate(parts):
   284	        if j % 2 == 1:                  # a bracketed anchor group: keep verbatim
   285	            out.append(part)
   286	        else:
   287	            out.append(part.replace("*", "").casefold())
   288	    joined = "".join(out)
   289	    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", joined).strip()

   293	    """The UTF-8 byte length of a criterion's full line text (the ratchet and budget unit)."""
   294	    return len(text.encode("utf-8"))

   297	def code_sort_key(code):
   298	    """A stable sort key for a code token: (prefix, first number)."""
   299	    m = re.match(r"([A-Z]+)-(\d+)", code)
   300	    return (m.group(1), int(m.group(2))) if m else (code, 0)

   303	def build_index_table(doc):
   304	    """The generated code-to-location table (SPEC INV-258): each code the body's criteria carry,
   305	    mapped to the requirement-and-criterion locations it appears at, sorted stably. Output only — this
   306	    is what `scripts/build-index.py` emits and the index gate rebuilds to compare. A range code like
   307	    `T-1..T-7` is carried whole, exactly as the criterion writes it."""
   308	    loc = {}
   309	    for c in doc.criteria:
   310	        where = "R%d.%d" % (c.req_num, c.number)
   311	        for code in c.codes:
   312	            loc.setdefault(code, [])
   313	            if where not in loc[code]:
   314	                loc[code].append(where)
   315	    rows = ["| Code | Location |", "|---|---|"]
   316	    for code in sorted(loc, key=code_sort_key):
   317	        rows.append("| %s | %s |" % (code, ", ".join(loc[code])))
   318	    return "\n".join(rows) + "\n"

   321	def index_table_codes(text):
   322	    """The set of codes in the first column of a committed code-to-location table."""
   323	    codes = set()
   324	    for line in text.split("\n"):
   325	        s = line.strip()
   326	        if not (s.startswith("|") and s.endswith("|")):
   327	            continue
   328	        cells = [c.strip() for c in s.strip("|").split("|")]
   329	        if not cells:
   330	            continue
   331	        first = cells[0]
   332	        if first.lower() == "code" or set(first) <= set("-: "):
   333	            continue
   334	        if CODE_RE.fullmatch(first):
   335	            codes.add(first)
   336	    return codes

   339	def body_codes(doc):
   340	    """The set of codes carried on the body's criteria."""
   341	    codes = set()
   342	    for c in doc.criteria:
   343	        codes.update(c.codes)
   344	    return codes

   347	def parts_map(text):
   348	    """The part files a core document's `## Parts map` table names, in concatenation order.
   349	
   350	    An empty list means what it says: this core is the whole document. The table's first column
   351	    carries the path, the rest (requirement range, topic) is for the reader; a header row and the
   352	    `|---|` rule are passed over, and the table ends at the next `## ` heading. The map stands in the
   353	    core's PREAMBLE, above the body, so the scan stops at the first requirement: a criterion that
   354	    quotes the heading is prose about the map, never the map."""
   355	    parts = []
   356	    in_map = False
   357	    for line in text.split("\n"):
   358	        s = line.strip()
   359	        if REQUIREMENT_RE.match(s):
   360	            break
   361	        if s == PARTS_MAP_HEAD:
   362	            in_map = True
   363	            continue
   364	        if not in_map:
   365	            continue
   366	        if s.startswith("## "):
   367	            break
   368	        if not (s.startswith("|") and s.endswith("|")):
   369	            continue
   370	        first = s.strip("|").split("|")[0].strip()
   371	        if set(first) <= set("-: ") or not first:
   372	            continue
   373	        m = PART_PATH_RE.search(first)
   374	        if m and m.group(0) not in parts:
   375	            parts.append(m.group(0))
   376	    return parts
   377

   379	def spec_paths(paths, root=None):
   380	    """The whole file list behind the documents named on a command line, in order, without repeats.
   381	
   382	    A named path that is a core carrying a parts map expands to that core followed by its parts,
   383	    resolved against `root` (default: the directory holding the core). Naming core and parts
   384	    explicitly is the same list — expansion is idempotent — so a caller may pass either, in either
   385	    spelling: sameness is decided on the resolved file, not on the string, so `spec/x.md` typed on a
   386	    command line and the absolute path the map expanded to are ONE file and are read once. Reading a
   387	    part twice would double every count built over the document, so this is the guard that keeps a
   388	    hand-typed command line honest. A path that cannot be read is returned as given, so the caller's
   389	    own missing-file red is what speaks."""
   390	    out, seen = [], set()
   391	    for p in paths:
   392	        for q in _expand(p, root):
   393	            key = os.path.realpath(q)
   394	            if key not in seen:
   395	                seen.add(key)
   396	                out.append(q)
   397	    return out
   398	
   399	
   400	def _expand(path, root):
   401	    try:
   402	        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
   403	            text = f.read()
   404	    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
   405	        return [path]
   406	    parts = parts_map(text)
   407	    if not parts:
   408	        return [path]
   409	    base = root if root is not None else os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
   410	    return [path] + [os.path.join(base, p) for p in parts]
   411	
   412	
   413	def read_document(paths, root=None, expand=True):
   414	    """`(resolved_paths, text)` for the documents named on a command line: the core and its parts
   415	    read as ONE text, in map order. With one path and no parts the text is that file's bytes
   416	    unchanged. Where a part does not end in a newline the join supplies one, so the last line of one
   417	    part and the first line of the next never fuse into a single line. `expand=False` reads the paths
   418	    exactly as given — for a caller that has already resolved them through `spec_paths`."""
   419	    resolved = spec_paths(paths, root) if expand else list(paths)
   420	    chunks = []
   421	    for p in resolved:
   422	        with open(p, encoding="utf-8") as f:
   423	            t = f.read()
   424	        if chunks and not chunks[-1].endswith("\n"):
   425	            chunks.append("\n")
   426	        chunks.append(t)
   427	    return resolved, "".join(chunks)

   430	def green_reach(check, files, matched, scanned, extra=""):
   431	    """The green line every gate in this family prints (SPEC INV-269): the verdict, the files it
   432	    opened, and the count of rows it matched of the rows it scanned — so a reader tells a real pass
   433	    from one that read nothing. A zero scanned count is never a bare green line; a gate reaches this
   434	    only after its require_nonempty guard has already red an empty input (INV-218), so `scanned` here
   435	    is non-zero by construction, and the reach states it plainly."""
   436	    names = ", ".join(files)
   437	    tail = ("; %s" % extra) if extra else ""
   438	    return ("%s: OK — reach: files=[%s]; matched %d of %d rows scanned%s"
   439	            % (check, names, matched, scanned, tail))

    20	  in exactly one case, trailing a code anchor at the line's end. A `[GAP: ...]` line may sit under it.
    21	- A criterion may carry a SUB-LIST: indented `- ` bullet lines directly under its numbered line, each
    22	  holding one more piece of that criterion's rule. The bullets belong to the criterion, so a gate
    23	  that reads a criterion's prose reads them too: `crit.bullets` holds them in order, and
    24	  `crit.pieces` returns the criterion's own body first and then each bullet. The sub-list ends at the
    25	  next criterion, the next case heading, the next requirement, or a blank line followed by
    26	  unindented text. Without this, moving words from a criterion line into bullets under it drops them
    27	  out of every prose gate's reach while the text a person reads stays the same length.
    28	
    29	The code anchor is one or more `[...]` groups at the line's end; a group holds codes like `INV-250`,
    30	`T-9`, `E-35`, `A-5`, `ACT-3`, or a range `T-1..T-7`, comma-separated, and may be preceded by a
    31	`[default]` marker. `[GAP: ...]` is a gap line, never a criterion.
    32	
    33	THE PARTS MAP. A document may be written as a CORE file plus PART files. The core carries the
    34	preamble, the glossary and a `## Parts map` table naming its parts in concatenation order; each part
    35	carries requirements only. The core is the single source of that order — nothing else lists the
    36	parts. A core with no map (or with an empty one) IS the whole document, which is the state this
    37	module ships in: `spec_paths(["PRODUCT_SPEC.md"])` returns exactly `["PRODUCT_SPEC.md"]` and
    38	`read_document` returns its bytes unchanged, so every reader behaves identically before and after the
    39	map exists. Readers call `read_document(paths)` rather than opening a path themselves, and the gates
    40	take a list of paths on the command line so a caller can name core and parts explicitly.

    42	Stdlib only.
    43	"""
    44	import os
    45	import re

    47	# A single code token: a letter-run, a dash, a number, with an optional range tail.
    48	CODE = r"[A-Z]+-[0-9]+(?:\.\.[A-Z]*-?[0-9]+)?"
    49	CODE_RE = re.compile(CODE)
    50	
    51	# A trailing anchor block: one or more bracket groups at the very end of a line, each holding codes
    52	# (or the bare `[default]` marker). `[GAP: ...]` is deliberately NOT an anchor.
    53	_BRACKET = r"\[[^\]]*\]"
    54	TRAILING_ANCHOR_RE = re.compile(r"(?:\s*%s)+\s*$" % _BRACKET)
    55	
    56	PARTS_MAP_HEAD = "## Parts map"
    57	# The path in a parts-map row's first cell. The path is READ OUT of the cell rather than required to
    58	# be the whole of it, so a cell written as a backticked path, a markdown link or a path with a note
    59	# after it still names its part: a row that silently named nothing would drop a part out of every
    60	# aggregate reader at once.
    61	PART_PATH_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_./-]*\.md")
    62	
    63	GLOSSARY_HEADS = ("## Glossary additions", "## Glossary")
    64	REQUIREMENT_RE = re.compile(r"^## Requirement\s+(\d+)\s*:\s*(.*)$")
    65	CASE_RE = re.compile(r"^\*\*Case:\s*(.+?)\s*\*\*\s*$")
    66	CONTEXT_RE = re.compile(r"^\*\*Context:\*\*")
    67	USER_STORY_RE = re.compile(r"^\*\*User Story:\*\*")
    68	AC_RE = re.compile(r"^###\s+Acceptance Criteria")
    69	CRITERION_RE = re.compile(r"^(\s*)(\d+)\.\s+(.*\S)\s*$")
    70	GAP_RE = re.compile(r"\[GAP:")
    71	GLOSSARY_TERM_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*-\s+\*\*(.+?)\*\*\s+—\s+(.*\S)\s*$")
    72	# A bullet of a criterion's sub-list: an indented `- ` line. The glossary's own `- **term**` lines
    73	# sit at column zero, so the indent is what separates the two.
    74	BULLET_RE = re.compile(r"^[ \t]+[-*+]\s+(.*\S)\s*$")
    75	
    76	# The label `pieces` gives a criterion's own body, so a gate can tell it from a bullet's label.
    77	CRITERION_LINE = "the criterion line"
    78	
    79	
    80	class Bullet(object):
    81	    """One indented bullet under a criterion line, carrying a piece of that criterion's rule."""
    82	
    83	    def __init__(self, text, line_no, index):
    84	        self.text = text                # the bullet's text after its `- ` marker
    85	        self.line_no = line_no          # 1-based source line
    86	        self.index = index              # 1-based position under its criterion
    87	
    88	    @property
    89	    def label(self):
    90	        """How a gate names this bullet to a writer."""
    91	        return "bullet %d" % self.index
    92

    94	class Criterion(object):
    95	    def __init__(self, req_num, number, text, line_no):
    96	        self.req_num = req_num          # the requirement number it sits under
    97	        self.number = number            # its own criterion number (int)
    98	        self.text = text                # the full criterion text after "N. "
    99	        self.line_no = line_no          # 1-based source line
   100	        self.case = None                # the case name it sits under (or None)
   101	        self.gap_lines = []             # any [GAP: ...] lines recorded beneath it
   102	        self.bullets = []               # Bullet objects of its sub-list, in order
   103	
   104	    @property
   105	    def codes(self):
   106	        """The distinct codes in this criterion's trailing anchor, ranges kept whole."""
   107	        anchor = self.anchor
   108	        return CODE_RE.findall(anchor) if anchor else []
   109	
   110	    @property
   111	    def anchor(self):
   112	        """The trailing anchor text, or '' when the criterion trails none."""
   113	        m = TRAILING_ANCHOR_RE.search(self.text)
   114	        if not m:
   115	            return ""
   116	        # A trailing `[GAP: ...]` on the criterion line itself is not an anchor.
   117	        chunk = m.group(0)
   118	        if "[GAP:" in chunk and not CODE_RE.search(chunk):
   119	            return ""
   120	        return chunk if CODE_RE.search(chunk) else ""
   121	
   122	    @property
   123	    def has_anchor(self):
   124	        return bool(self.anchor)
   125	
   126	    @property
   127	    def body(self):
   128	        """The criterion text with its trailing anchor stripped."""
   129	        a = self.anchor
   130	        return self.text[: self.text.rfind(a)].rstrip() if a else self.text
   131	
   132	    @property
   133	    def pieces(self):
   134	        """The criterion's sentences in reading order: its own body first, then each bullet of its
   135	        sub-list. Each piece is `(label, text, line_no)`. A gate that measures a criterion's prose
   136	        measures every piece, so words moved from the line into a bullet stay in reach."""
   137	        out = [(CRITERION_LINE, self.body, self.line_no)]
   138	        for b in self.bullets:
   139	            out.append((b.label, b.text, b.line_no))
   140	        return out

   143	class Requirement(object):
   144	    def __init__(self, number, title, line_no):
   145	        self.number = number
   146	        self.title = title
   147	        self.line_no = line_no
   148	        self.has_context = False
   149	        self.has_user_story = False
   150	        self.has_ac = False
   151	        self.cases = []                 # ordered case names
   152	        self.criteria = []              # Criterion objects, in order
   153	
   154	
   155	class Document(object):
   156	    def __init__(self):
   157	        self.preamble = ""
   158	        self.glossary_head = None       # the heading text used, or None
   159	        self.glossary = []              # list of (term, definition, line_no) in order
   160	        self.requirements = []          # Requirement objects
   161	        self.text = ""
   162	
   163	    @property
   164	    def glossary_terms(self):
   165	        return [t for (t, _d, _l) in self.glossary]
   166	
   167	    @property
   168	    def criteria(self):
   169	        out = []
   170	        for r in self.requirements:
   171	            out.extend(r.criteria)

   175	def parse(text):
   176	    """Parse a requirements-format document into a Document. Tolerant: unknown lines are ignored, so
   177	    a partly-formed document still yields the structure the gates can red against."""
   178	    doc = Document()
   179	    doc.text = text
   180	    lines = text.split("\n")
   181	
   182	    # Locate the glossary heading (the first of the two forms that appears).
   183	    gloss_idx = None
   184	    for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
   185	        s = ln.strip()
   186	        if s in GLOSSARY_HEADS:
   187	            gloss_idx = i
   188	            doc.glossary_head = s
   189	            break
   190	
   191	    # Preamble: everything before the glossary heading (or before the first requirement if no
   192	    # glossary heading is present).
   193	    first_req = None
   194	    for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
   195	        if REQUIREMENT_RE.match(ln.strip()):
   196	            first_req = i
   197	            break
   198	    cut = gloss_idx if gloss_idx is not None else (first_req if first_req is not None else len(lines))
   199	    doc.preamble = "\n".join(lines[:cut]).strip()
   200	
   201	    # Glossary terms: from the glossary heading up to the first requirement (or the next `## ` head).
   202	    if gloss_idx is not None:
   203	        for i in range(gloss_idx + 1, len(lines)):
   204	            s = lines[i].strip()
   205	            if REQUIREMENT_RE.match(s) or (s.startswith("## ") and s not in GLOSSARY_HEADS):
   206	                break
   207	            m = GLOSSARY_TERM_RE.match(lines[i])
   208	            if m:
   209	                doc.glossary.append((m.group(1).strip(), m.group(2).strip(), i + 1))
   210	
   211	    # Requirements, cases, criteria.
   212	    cur_req = None
   213	    cur_case = None
   214	    in_ac = False
   215	    last_crit = None
   216	    bullet_owner = None                 # the criterion whose sub-list is open here
   217	    prev_blank = True
   218	    for i, raw in enumerate(lines):
   219	        s = raw.strip()
   220	        if not s:
   221	            prev_blank = True
   222	            continue
   223	        if prev_blank and raw[:1] not in (" ", "\t"):
   224	            # A blank line and then unindented text close the open sub-list.
   225	            bullet_owner = None
   226	        prev_blank = False
   227	        mreq = REQUIREMENT_RE.match(s)
   228	        if mreq:
   229	            cur_req = Requirement(int(mreq.group(1)), mreq.group(2).strip(), i + 1)
   230	            doc.requirements.append(cur_req)
   231	            cur_case = None
   232	            in_ac = False
   233	            last_crit = None
   234	            bullet_owner = None
   235	            continue
   236	        if cur_req is None:
   237	            continue
   238	        if CONTEXT_RE.match(s):
   239	            cur_req.has_context = True
   240	            continue
   241	        if USER_STORY_RE.match(s):
   242	            cur_req.has_user_story = True
   243	            continue
   244	        if AC_RE.match(s):
   245	            cur_req.has_ac = True
   246	            in_ac = True
   247	            continue
   248	        mcase = CASE_RE.match(s)
   249	        if mcase:
   250	            cur_case = mcase.group(1).strip()
   251	            cur_req.cases.append(cur_case)
   252	            last_crit = None
   253	            bullet_owner = None
   254	            continue
   255	        # A [GAP: ...] line attaches to the criterion above it.
   256	        if GAP_RE.search(s) and CRITERION_RE.match(raw) is None:
   257	            if last_crit is not None:
   258	                last_crit.gap_lines.append(s)
   259	            continue
   260	        mcrit = CRITERION_RE.match(raw)
   261	        if mcrit and in_ac:
   262	            crit = Criterion(cur_req.number, int(mcrit.group(2)), mcrit.group(3).strip(), i + 1)
   263	            crit.case = cur_case
   264	            cur_req.criteria.append(crit)
   265	            last_crit = crit
   266	            bullet_owner = crit
   267	            continue
   268	        # An indented bullet under an open criterion is a piece of that criterion.
   269	        mbul = BULLET_RE.match(raw)
   270	        if mbul and bullet_owner is not None:
   271	            bullet_owner.bullets.append(
   272	                Bullet(mbul.group(1).strip(), i + 1, len(bullet_owner.bullets) + 1))
   273	            continue
   274	    return doc

   277	def normalize_criterion(text):
   278	    """The delta-classifier normal form (SPEC INV-261): whitespace collapsed, italic `*` markers
   279	    stripped, letters case-folded OUTSIDE code anchors — so a `[INV-4]` anchor keeps its case while
   280	    the sentence around it folds. Bracketed groups are held verbatim, the rest is folded."""
   281	    parts = re.split(r"(\[[^\]]*\])", text)
   282	    out = []
   283	    for j, part in enumerate(parts):
   284	        if j % 2 == 1:                  # a bracketed anchor group: keep verbatim
   285	            out.append(part)
   286	        else:
   287	            out.append(part.replace("*", "").casefold())
   288	    joined = "".join(out)
   289	    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", joined).strip()

   292	def criterion_bytes(text):
   293	    """The UTF-8 byte length of a criterion's full line text (the ratchet and budget unit)."""
   294	    return len(text.encode("utf-8"))
   295	
   296	
   297	def code_sort_key(code):
   298	    """A stable sort key for a code token: (prefix, first number)."""
   299	    m = re.match(r"([A-Z]+)-(\d+)", code)
   300	    return (m.group(1), int(m.group(2))) if m else (code, 0)
   301	
   302	
   303	def build_index_table(doc):
   304	    """The generated code-to-location table (SPEC INV-258): each code the body's criteria carry,
   305	    mapped to the requirement-and-criterion locations it appears at, sorted stably. Output only — this
   306	    is what `scripts/build-index.py` emits and the index gate rebuilds to compare. A range code like
   307	    `T-1..T-7` is carried whole, exactly as the criterion writes it."""
   308	    loc = {}
   309	    for c in doc.criteria:
   310	        where = "R%d.%d" % (c.req_num, c.number)
   311	        for code in c.codes:
   312	            loc.setdefault(code, [])
   313	            if where not in loc[code]:
   314	                loc[code].append(where)
   315	    rows = ["| Code | Location |", "|---|---|"]
   316	    for code in sorted(loc, key=code_sort_key):
   317	        rows.append("| %s | %s |" % (code, ", ".join(loc[code])))
   318	    return "\n".join(rows) + "\n"

   321	def index_table_codes(text):
   322	    """The set of codes in the first column of a committed code-to-location table."""
   323	    codes = set()
   324	    for line in text.split("\n"):
   325	        s = line.strip()
   326	        if not (s.startswith("|") and s.endswith("|")):
   327	            continue
   328	        cells = [c.strip() for c in s.strip("|").split("|")]
   329	        if not cells:
   330	            continue
   331	        first = cells[0]
   332	        if first.lower() == "code" or set(first) <= set("-: "):
   333	            continue
   334	        if CODE_RE.fullmatch(first):
   335	            codes.add(first)
   336	    return codes

   339	def body_codes(doc):
   340	    """The set of codes carried on the body's criteria."""
   341	    codes = set()
   342	    for c in doc.criteria:
   343	        codes.update(c.codes)
   344	    return codes

   347	def parts_map(text):
   348	    """The part files a core document's `## Parts map` table names, in concatenation order.
   349	
   350	    An empty list means what it says: this core is the whole document. The table's first column
   351	    carries the path, the rest (requirement range, topic) is for the reader; a header row and the
   352	    `|---|` rule are passed over, and the table ends at the next `## ` heading. The map stands in the
   353	    core's PREAMBLE, above the body, so the scan stops at the first requirement: a criterion that
   354	    quotes the heading is prose about the map, never the map."""
   355	    parts = []
   356	    in_map = False
   357	    for line in text.split("\n"):
   358	        s = line.strip()
   359	        if REQUIREMENT_RE.match(s):
   360	            break
   361	        if s == PARTS_MAP_HEAD:
   362	            in_map = True
   363	            continue
   364	        if not in_map:
   365	            continue
   366	        if s.startswith("## "):
   367	            break
   368	        if not (s.startswith("|") and s.endswith("|")):
   369	            continue
   370	        first = s.strip("|").split("|")[0].strip()
   371	        if set(first) <= set("-: ") or not first:
   372	            continue
   373	        m = PART_PATH_RE.search(first)
   374	        if m and m.group(0) not in parts:
   375	            parts.append(m.group(0))
   376	    return parts

   379	def spec_paths(paths, root=None):
   380	    """The whole file list behind the documents named on a command line, in order, without repeats.
   381	
   382	    A named path that is a core carrying a parts map expands to that core followed by its parts,
   383	    resolved against `root` (default: the directory holding the core). Naming core and parts
   384	    explicitly is the same list — expansion is idempotent — so a caller may pass either, in either
   385	    spelling: sameness is decided on the resolved file, not on the string, so `spec/x.md` typed on a
   386	    command line and the absolute path the map expanded to are ONE file and are read once. Reading a
   387	    part twice would double every count built over the document, so this is the guard that keeps a
   388	    hand-typed command line honest. A path that cannot be read is returned as given, so the caller's
   389	    own missing-file red is what speaks."""
   390	    out, seen = [], set()
   391	    for p in paths:
   392	        for q in _expand(p, root):
   393	            key = os.path.realpath(q)
   394	            if key not in seen:
   395	                seen.add(key)
   396	                out.append(q)
   397	    return out
   398	
   399	
   400	def _expand(path, root):
   401	    try:
   402	        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
   403	            text = f.read()
   404	    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
   405	        return [path]
   406	    parts = parts_map(text)
   407	    if not parts:
   408	        return [path]
   409	    base = root if root is not None else os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
   410	    return [path] + [os.path.join(base, p) for p in parts]
   411	
   412	
   413	def read_document(paths, root=None, expand=True):
   414	    """`(resolved_paths, text)` for the documents named on a command line: the core and its parts
   415	    read as ONE text, in map order. With one path and no parts the text is that file's bytes
   416	    unchanged. Where a part does not end in a newline the join supplies one, so the last line of one
   417	    part and the first line of the next never fuse into a single line. `expand=False` reads the paths
   418	    exactly as given — for a caller that has already resolved them through `spec_paths`."""
   419	    resolved = spec_paths(paths, root) if expand else list(paths)
   420	    chunks = []
   421	    for p in resolved:
   422	        with open(p, encoding="utf-8") as f:
   423	            t = f.read()
   424	        if chunks and not chunks[-1].endswith("\n"):
   425	            chunks.append("\n")
   426	        chunks.append(t)
   427	    return resolved, "".join(chunks)
   428	
   429	
   430	def green_reach(check, files, matched, scanned, extra=""):
   431	    """The green line every gate in this family prints (SPEC INV-269): the verdict, the files it
   432	    opened, and the count of rows it matched of the rows it scanned — so a reader tells a real pass
   433	    from one that read nothing. A zero scanned count is never a bare green line; a gate reaches this
   434	    only after its require_nonempty guard has already red an empty input (INV-218), so `scanned` here
   435	    is non-zero by construction, and the reach states it plainly."""
   436	    names = ", ".join(files)
   437	    tail = ("; %s" % extra) if extra else ""
   438	    return ("%s: OK — reach: files=[%s]; matched %d of %d rows scanned%s"
   439	            % (check, names, matched, scanned, tail))
